sentences.text:
The petitioner challenged the said Award on the following grounds:-
i) The petitioner did not receive any notice of the notification as well as the award from the LAC.
The petitioner did not get the opportunity to file his objections before the LAC against the award since he had not received any notice of the award in question.
Other than petitioner, no other person has any right, title or interest in the shop and only petitioner is entitled to compensation/ enhanced compensation.

The petitioner is not satisfied with the compensation amount awarded by the LAC,
determination of market value of land in question, measurement of land etc.
ii) The LAC has mistakenly assessed the market value LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 3 of 14 of land of petitioner at low rates which does not represents the market value of the land on the date of notification U/s 4 of LA,
Act.
iii) The LAC admitted that the land in question was surrounded by commercial and thickly populated colonies like Jheel Khuranja, Geeta Colony etc.

entities.text: LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Despite the same,
the LAC passed the award without making any on spot inquiry and without considering the principle of demand and supply.
The area in question was declared local commercial area by MCD.
iv) The LAC completely ignored the interests of the petitioner and given the amount to those who are not even the owners of the land.
v) In addition, LAC has failed to appreciate that a lot of development took place in the proximity of land in question like construction of flyover, banks, commercial complexes, railway station etc.
The acquired land has higher potential market value than granted by the LAC.
The LAC has valued the land in question @ Rs.2805/- per sq.mt. only whereas the market value was not less than Rs.50,000/- sq.yds.

The LAC has not taken into consideration the market rates of Jheel Khuranja and Geeta Colony (adjoining areas) while passing the award and the market rates of Narela has been considered by LAC which is approximately 30 kms away from the acquired land.
vi) In view of the above reasons, this reference was filed by the petitioner before this Court.

sentences.text: It is averred in the written statement filed on behalf of Land Acquisition Collector (Shahdara)/respondent No.1 that notification U/s 4 of Act was issued on 12.06.1997 for acquisition of 41 bigha land.
The declaration U/s 6 & 17 of the Act were issued on 28.07.1997.
The land has been acquired for the public purpose namely Mass Rapid Transit System Project.

Notices U/s 9 & 10 were issued to the land owners/interested persons, inviting claims of the affected properties and in pursuance thereof, number of claims were filed by the affected persons, claiming different value of the land and properties.
Necessary demarcation was carried out at the spot and it was revealed that total area was 39 bigha and 10 biswas instead of 41 bigha, as shown in notification U/ 4 & 6 of Act.
There was difference of 1 bigha and 10 biswa, as the actual area of khasra was 12 bigha and 6 biswa.

After considering all the claims, LAC had made and announced the award U/s 11 of LA Act bearing No.1/1999-2000 on 20.07.1999.
6.)
The claim of the petitioner with respect to measurements, apportionment and compensation of land is admitted to the extent of section 19 statement of LAC.
The compensation assessed by LAC is sufficient and reasonable and it reflects the true market value prevailing at the time of notification issued U/s 4 of Act.

Various factors were taken into account while assessing the market value,
previous award of the same village and also gave due appreciation to assess the market value of the land for the corresponding period.
LAC has assessed fair market value of the LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 5 of 14 land @ Rs.2850 per sq. meter besides other statutory benefits.

The LAC has considered the market value of the land on the date of publication of notification U/s 4 of Act i.e. 12.06.1997.
The Slum Area Improvement and Clearance Act is applicable to the land in dispute.

sentences.text: None of the parties had filed any evidence to support their claim and after denying other averments, it has prayed for dismissal of the reference petition with heavy costs.
7.) It is averred in the written statement filed, on behalf of DMRC i.e. respondent No.2 that compensation has been correctly assessed by the LAC.
Petitioner is not entitled for enhanced compensation on the land in question.
LAC has taken into consideration all the factors including location and potentiality of the land while assessing the market value of the land.
The present reference petition is filed beyond the period of limitation and therefore, liable to be dismissed with cost.

8.) Accordingly, Issue-wise findings are as follows:-
(V) Issue-Wise Findings:-
Issue no.1: Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement of amount of compensation?

(OPP)
a) Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.

In support of their respective shares, petitioners have relied upon Ex.PW1/1 (judgment U/s 30-31, L.A. Act dated 09.01.2008 passed by Sh.
Sanjay Kumar, Ld. ADJ, Tis Hazari Courts).

b) As per the judgment, the petitioners- Sh. Sudhir Saran Bhatnagar, Sh. Sunil Bhatnagar and Smt.
Sudha Prasad were held entitled for compensation for the land measuring 1 bigha 2.5 biswas in respect of Khasra nos.984/446 (0-16.5) and 1114/991/450 (0-6).

The relevant para of the said judgment is reproduced herein:-
"In view of my findings on issue no.1, LRs of Lt. Sh. Sukhbir Saran viz. Sudhir LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 10 of 14 Saran, Sudha Prasad and Sunil Bhatnagar are entitled for land compensation for the land measuring 1 bigha and 2.5 biswas in respect of Khasra No.984/446 (0-16.5) and 1114/991/450 (0-6) to the extent of 1/3rd equal shares".

c) Further, during the course of argument, parties have apprised this Court that the market value with respect to the property in question acquired vide the same notification and same award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 07.06.2019 passed in the case titled as "Union of India Vs. M.L. Gupta & Ors.' in which the Hon'ble High Court has fixed the market value of the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award @ Rs.4692/-
per sq.mtr. along-with statutory benefits.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court has assessed the said market value after allowing a reduction of 20% @ Rs.5865/- per sq.mtr. which was previously determined by my Ld. Predecessor.

d) Since there is an authoritative pronouncement on the fair market value of the similar land placed in similar circumstances, location and topography and acquired vide the same award, this Court need not to delve further in this regard.
Even otherwise, two equals cannot be treated unequally.

Reliance in this regard can be placed upon the judgment titled as 'Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. Vs.
State of J&K' reported in AIR 2017 SC 1518 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court wherein it is held that "when the acquired lands are identical and similar and the LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs.
Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 11 of 14 acquisition is for the same purpose, it would not be proper to discriminate between the land owners unless there are strong reasons".

e) Though respondent no.2- DMRC argued that the SLP is still pending before the Hon'ble Supreme Court with respect to the determination of market value, however from the perusal of the record, it is observed that SLP filed by the respondents has been dismissed, however, SLP filed by the petitioner, namely, Sh. M.L. Gupta is still pending adjudication.
Thus, market value assessed by the Hon'ble High Court has reached finality qua the respondents.
Thus, this issue is decided in favuor of the petitioner.
Issue no.2: Relief.
a) In view of the findings on issue no.1, the petition/ reference filed U/s 18 of L.A. Act, is answered.
The petitioners had claimed compensation of Rs.50,000/- per sq.metre, which is LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 12 of 14 now fixed and allowed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.metre.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners are entitled to the fair market value @ Rs.4692/- per sq.metre. as on 12.06.1997 with respect to the share determined in the land acquired i.e. 1 bigha 2.5 biswas as per the judgment in reference U/s 30-31, L.A. Act dated 09.01.2008.
b) According to the awards, solatium was allowed @ 30%.
Accordingly, the solatium is also allowed @ 30% on the market value, as determined above, as per provisions of L.A. Act, 1894.
c) The petitioners have also claimed interest, as per law.

According to the award, 12% interest was allowed on the market value, fixed by the LAC U/s 23(1)A of LA Act, 1894 from the date of notification U/s 4 of Act (12.06.1997) till the date of dispossession i.e. 20.07.1999.
Accordingly, the same is also allowed on the present market value, fixed as above.

d) According to the award, interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894 was also allowed observing that DMRC had taken the land and as such petitioners are entitled to interest on the balance amount, as per section 34 of LA Act, 1894 @ 9% per annum from the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999 till expiry of one year and thereafter, @ 15% per annum till payment or deposited into the Court.
The same is also allowed on the enhanced market value of the land in question, as determined above.
The respondent nos.1 and 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation as determined hereinabove to the petitioner/ LRs of petitioner.

e) The above reliefs are subject to the deductions of LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 13 of 14 compensation / solatium / additional benefits / interest U/s 34 of LA Act,
1894, which have already been received by the petitioner, as were fixed by the LAC vide Award No.
01/1999- 2000 dated 20.07.1999.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner challenged the said Award on the following grounds:-
i) The petitioner did not receive any notice of the notification as well as the award from the LAC.
The petitioner did not get the opportunity to file his objections before the LAC against the award since he had not received any notice of the award in question.
Other than petitioner, no other person has any right, title or interest in the shop and only petitioner is entitled to compensation/ enhanced compensation.
The petitioner is not satisfied with the compensation amount awarded by the LAC,
determination of market value of land in question, measurement of land etc.
ii) The LAC has mistakenly assessed the market value LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 3 of 14 of land of petitioner at low rates which does not represents the market value of the land on the date of notification U/s 4 of LA,
Act.
iii) The LAC admitted that the land in question was surrounded by commercial and thickly populated colonies like Jheel Khuranja, Geeta Colony etc.
Despite the same,
the LAC passed the award without making any on spot inquiry and without considering the principle of demand and supply.
The compensation assessed by LAC is sufficient and reasonable and it reflects the true market value prevailing at the time of notification issued U/s 4 of Act.
Various factors were taken into account while assessing the market value,
previous award of the same village and also gave due appreciation to assess the market value of the land for the corresponding period.
LAC has assessed fair market value of the LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 5 of 14 land @ Rs.2850 per sq. meter besides other statutory benefits.
The petitioners have claimed excessive and exorbitant market value of the land and structures.
Petitioner is not entitled for enhanced compensation on the land in question.
LAC has taken into consideration all the factors including location and potentiality of the land while assessing the market value of the land.
8.) During pendency of the proceedings, petitioner had expired and application U/o 22 rule 3 CPC was filed along-with another application U/s 5 of Limitation Act, which were allowed vide order dated 04.02.2013 and all the three LR's of deceased petitioner were impleaded as petitioners in the present case.
The Hon'ble High Court has assessed the said market value after allowing a reduction of 20% @ Rs.5865/- per sq.mtr. which was previously determined by my Ld. Predecessor.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Issue no.1: Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement of amount of compensation?
c) Further, during the course of argument, parties have apprised this Court that the market value with respect to the property in question acquired vide the same notification and same award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 07.06.2019 passed in the case titled as "Union of India Vs. M.L. Gupta & Ors.' in which the Hon'ble High Court has fixed the market value of the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award @ Rs.4692/-
per sq.mtr. along-with statutory benefits.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
d) Since there is an authoritative pronouncement on the fair market value of the similar land placed in similar circumstances, location and topography and acquired vide the same award, this Court need not to delve further in this regard.
Even otherwise, two equals cannot be treated unequally.
In these circumstances, this Court is not inclined to go into any evidences or judgments relied upon by the parties to the instant petition in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court in case titled as 'Union of India Sukhbir Saran vs Union Of India on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187233656/
7 Vs. M.L. Gupta' wherein the market value for the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award have already been assessed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e.
12.06.1997.
Even otherwise, nothing substantial has been brought on record by either side to differ from the market value assessed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in one of the matters arising out of the same award and pertaining to the identical land.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners had claimed compensation of Rs.50,000/- per sq.metre, which is LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 12 of 14 now fixed and allowed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.metre.
The petitioners are entitled to the fair market value @ Rs.4692/- per sq.metre. as on 12.06.1997 with respect to the share determined in the land acquired i.e. 1 bigha 2.5 biswas as per the judgment in reference U/s 30-31, L.A. Act dated 09.01.2008.
Accordingly, the same is also allowed on the present market value, fixed as above.
d) According to the award, interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894 was also allowed observing that DMRC had taken the land and as such petitioners are entitled to interest on the balance amount, as per section 34 of LA Act, 1894 @ 9% per annum from the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999 till expiry of one year and thereafter, @ 15% per annum till payment or deposited into the Court.
The same is also allowed on the enhanced market value of the land in question, as determined above.
The respondent nos.1 and 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation as determined hereinabove to the petitioner/ LRs of petitioner.
e) The above reliefs are subject to the deductions of LAC No.52/16 Sukhbir Saran Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 13 of 14 compensation / solatium / additional benefits / interest U/s 34 of LA Act,
1894, which have already been received by the petitioner, as were fixed by the LAC vide Award No.
01/1999- 2000 dated 20.07.1999.
Sukhbir Saran vs Union Of India on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187233656/
8 f)
The reference petition stands answered accordingly.
Both the parties will bear their own costs.
A copy of this judgment be sent to LAC concerned to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation to the petitioners within three months from today.
No order as to cost.
